root.label: The Great War, 1914–1919
root.gloss: Voluntary enlistment, Western Front trenches and General Haig, forgotten colonial troops, Britain’s Home Front, and Versailles.

children.label: Part 1: Enlistment & Trenches
children.gloss: Why British men rushed to volunteer in 1914, trench stalemate, the 1 July 1916 Somme disaster, and the Haig debate.

children.label: 1. 1914 Rush to the Colours
children.gloss: Kitchener’s appeal, outrage over Belgium, Pals Battalions, working-class poverty, and coercive White Feather pressure.

children.label: Kitchener’s Call & Belgium
children.gloss: Entering war with just 120,000 regular soldiers, Kitchener called for 500,000 volunteers amid fury over occupied Belgium.

children.label: Tiny 120,000 Professional British Army
children.gloss: Britain had zero conscription laws; Kitchener called for 500,000 volunteers.

children.label: Belgian Atrocities & Louvain Fire
children.gloss: Broke 1839 Treaty of London; Burned historic Louvain library.

children.label: → Flooded Recruitment Offices Nationwide
children.gloss: Framed war as moral crusade; Shattered quick-war government assumptions.

children.label: Built Mass Citizen Volunteer Army
children.gloss: Matched continental conscript armies; Relied on voluntary civic duty.

children.label: Pals Battalions & Poverty
children.gloss: Local Pals Battalions and guaranteed army pay drew working-class recruits hoping the war would end by Christmas.

children.label: Pals Battalions & Pompey Pals
children.gloss: Friends and neighbours trained together; Formed 14th/15th Hants Pompey Pals.

children.label: King’s Shilling Escaped Poverty
children.gloss: Guaranteed regular pay, food, boots; Believed war over by Christmas.

children.label: → Exposed Whole Towns to Loss
children.gloss: Boosted early battalion morale strongly; One battle devastated entire streets.

children.label: Blended Comradeship With Economic Need
children.gloss: Escaped damp tenements and factories; Civic pride drove mass enlistment.

children.label: Posters & White Feathers
children.gloss: Pointing Kitchener posters and public shaming by the White Feather Movement coerced hesitant men into uniform.

children.label: Kitchener’s Pointing Finger Poster
children.gloss: Demanded duty for King, country; Stared directly at civilian passers-by.

children.label: Public White Feather Shaming
children.gloss: Handed white feathers as cowardice; Targeted men in civilian clothes.

children.label: → Pressured Reluctant Men to Enlist
children.gloss: Made civilian clothes unbearable shame; Sustained volunteer numbers into 1915.

children.label: Revealed Coercive Wartime Culture
children.gloss: Patriotism mixed pride with humiliation; Foreshadowed 1916 compulsory conscription.

children.label: 2. Trenches, Somme & Haig
children.gloss: 400 miles of zig-zag trenches, trench foot and shell shock, 57,470 casualties on 1 July 1916, and the Haig debate.

children.label: 400-Mile Trench Stalemate
children.gloss: Machine guns and artillery forced armies into a three-tier, 400-mile trench system plagued by trench foot and shell shock.

children.label: Race to Sea & Machine Guns
children.gloss: Open movement swept by shrapnel; 400 miles Channel to Switzerland.

children.label: Three-Tier Zig-Zag Trench Lines
children.gloss: Sandbag traverses blocked straight fire; Deep barbed wire, 30ft dugouts.

children.label: → Trench Foot & Shell Shock
children.gloss: Flooded mud caused fungal amputations; Heavy shelling shattered soldiers’ nerves.

children.label: Gave Defenders Lethal Advantage
children.gloss: Wire funnelled infantry into guns; Created grinding war of attrition.

children.label: 1 July 1916 Somme Catastrophe
children.gloss: After a 1.5-million-shell bombardment failed to cut German wire, British forces suffered 57,470 casualties on 1 July 1916.

children.label: Offensive to Relieve French Verdun
children.gloss: 7-day, 1.5-million-shell artillery barrage; Haig expected obliterated German lines.

children.label: 57,470 Casualties on Day One
children.gloss: Shrapnel shells left wire intact; Germans emerged from deep dugouts.

children.label: → Decimated Volunteer Pals Units
children.gloss: Mowed down crossing No Man’s Land; Bloodiest day in British history.

children.label: Mowed down crossing No Man’s Land
children.gloss: Mowed down crossing No Man’s Land

children.label: Shattered Pre-War Tactical Beliefs
children.gloss: Exposed limits of shrapnel barrages; Forced urgent battlefield innovation.

children.label: The General Haig Debate
children.gloss: Historians clash between condemning Haig as the "Butcher of the Somme" and crediting his 1918 combined-arms learning curve.

children.label: Traditional: Callous Butcher in Mud
children.gloss: Lions led by aristocratic donkeys; Squandered lives in frontal attacks.

children.label: Modern: Industrial Learning Curve
children.gloss: No general knew trench solutions; Adapted tactics through hard lessons.

children.label: → Forged 1918 Combined-Arms Tactics
children.gloss: Coordinated tanks and creeping barrages; Integrated aircraft for 1918 victory.

children.label: Sharpest British Command Controversy
children.gloss: Weighs 1916 slaughter against 1918; Shows how historians revise verdicts.

children.label: Part 2: Empire & Home Front
children.gloss: Four million colonial and dominion personnel, Gallipoli, Chinese labourers, DORA, conscription, Canary Girls, and rationing.

children.label: 3. Empire & Forgotten Fronts
children.gloss: Indian troops at Ypres, ANZACs at Gallipoli, the Chinese Labour Corps, and post-war erasure of African and Asian sacrifice.

children.label: Imperial Lifeline & First Ypres
children.gloss: Over four million colonial and dominion personnel mobilised as the Indian Corps helped save Flanders in autumn 1914.

children.label: Four Million Imperial Personnel
children.gloss: Mobilised troops across five continents; Ships brought colonial wheat, oil.

children.label: Indian Corps & Khudadad Khan VC
children.gloss: Held freezing Ypres in cotton; First Asian Victoria Cross winner.

children.label: → Blocked 1914 German Breakthrough
children.gloss: Reinforced exhausted regular British units; 1.3m Indians served across war.

children.label: Made Allied Victory Globally Imperial
children.gloss: Prevented Allied economic collapse; Sustained Europe, Mesopotamia, Palestine.

children.label: Gallipoli & Labour Battalions
children.gloss: ANZAC troops endured eight months at Gallipoli while 140,000 Chinese Labour Corps workers sustained Allied logistics under segregation.

children.label: 1915 Anzac Cove Stalemate
children.gloss: Pinned below cliffs by Ottomans; Evacuated after eight bloody months.

children.label: 140,000 Chinese Labour Corps
children.gloss: Dug trenches, unloaded toxic shells; Locked inside segregated curfew camps.

children.label: → Forged ANZAC Pride & Logistics
children.gloss: Birthed lasting ANZAC national identity; Kept Western Front railways running.

children.label: Exposed Wartime Racial Hierarchies
children.gloss: Chinese barred from French civilians; Vital war work met prejudice.

children.label: Unmarked Graves & Erasure
children.gloss: Over one million African porters died without individual headstones and non-white troops were barred from London’s 1919 Victory Parade.

children.label: One Million African Porters Died
children.gloss: Carried supplies across East Africa; Buried in anonymous unmarked pits.

children.label: Barred From 1919 Victory Parade
children.gloss: Excluded non-white colonial regiments; Denied equal post-war war pensions.

children.label: → Erased Colonial Memory for Decades
children.gloss: White troops received named headstones; Hid empire’s sacrifice from textbooks.

children.label: Institutionalised Post-War Inequality
children.gloss: Exposed double standard of empire; Now recovered by modern historians.

children.label: 4. Home Front & Total War
children.gloss: DORA emergency powers, the 1915 shell scandal, 1916 conscription, female Canary Girls, and 1918 rationing against U-boats.

children.label: DORA & 1915 Shell Crisis
children.gloss: Parliament passed DORA in August 1914 and created Lloyd George’s Ministry of Munitions after the May 1915 shell famine.

children.label: Aug 1914 DORA State Controls
children.gloss: Censored press and casualty news; Cut pub hours, watered beer.

children.label: May 1915 Daily Mail Shell Scandal
children.gloss: Frontline shortage of explosive shells; Forced Asquith into coalition government.

children.label: → Lloyd George Ran State Factories
children.gloss: Created powerful Ministry of Munitions; Nationalised private arms production.

children.label: Replaced Laissez-Faire With Total War
children.gloss: Suspended Victorian liberal freedoms; Directed land, labour, and factories.

children.label: Conscription & Canary Girls
children.gloss: Parliament introduced conscription in January 1916 while nearly one million female munitions workers produced 80% of British shells.

children.label: Jan 1916 Military Service Act
children.gloss: Conscripted unmarried men aged 18–41; 16,000 conscientious objectors refused.

children.label: Canary Girls Made 80% of Shells
children.gloss: Toxic TNT yellowed skin, hair; 1917 Silvertown blast killed 73.

children.label: → Sustained Mass Frontline Firepower
children.gloss: Nearly one million women worked; Ended 1915 artillery shell famine.

children.label: Reshaped State Duty & Gender Roles
children.gloss: First compulsory British army call-up; Strengthened claim for women’s vote.

children.label: U-Boats & 1918 Ration Books
children.gloss: Unrestricted German U-boat warfare cut Britain’s wheat to six weeks in 1917 until naval convoys and 1918 rationing defeated starvation.

children.label: 1917 Unrestricted U-Boat Campaign
children.gloss: Sank merchant ships across Atlantic; Left six weeks wheat reserve.

children.label: Early 1918 Compulsory Ration Books
children.gloss: Rationed sugar, meat, butter, jam; Ended grocer queues and panic.

children.label: → Convoys & Rations Beat Blockade
children.gloss: Allied naval convoys protected ships; Guaranteed fair civilian food shares.

children.label: Kept British Home Morale Intact
children.gloss: Avoided German-style hunger collapse; Outlasted Central Powers into 1918.

children.label: Part 3: Armistice & Versailles
children.gloss: German naval mutiny and the 1918 Armistice, the clash of the Big Three in Paris, Article 231, and the Versailles verdict.

children.label: 5. Versailles & Flawed Peace
children.gloss: From the 11 November 1918 Compiègne Armistice to Article 231, £6.6bn reparations, Keynes’s warning, and 1930s enforcement failure.

children.label: 1918 Collapse & Big Three Aims
children.gloss: Kiel mutinies forced the 11 November 1918 Armistice before Wilson, Clemenceau, and Lloyd George clashed at Paris.

children.label: Kiel Mutiny & 11 Nov Armistice
children.gloss: Sailors mutinied; Kaiser fled Holland; Signed inside Compiègne rail carriage.

children.label: Wilson vs Clemenceau vs Lloyd George
children.gloss: Wilson: 14 Points and League; Clemenceau: revenge; UK wanted trade.

children.label: → Forged Uneasy June 1919 Compromise
children.gloss: Moderated French dismemberment demands; Excluded defeated Germany from talks.

children.label: Satisfied None of the Peacemakers
children.gloss: Too harsh for German reconciliation; Too soft to crush German power.

children.label: Too soft to crush German power
children.gloss: Too soft to crush German power

children.label: Article 231 & Punitive Diktat
children.gloss: Versailles imposed War Guilt (Article 231), £6.6bn reparations, 13% land loss, and a 100,000-man army cap on Weimar Germany.

children.label: Article 231 & £6.6bn Reparations
children.gloss: Forced total moral war blame; Imposed £6.6bn reparations bill.

children.label: Lost 13% Land & 100,000 Army Cap
children.gloss: Lost colonies; Rhineland was demilitarised; Banned conscription and combat planes.

children.label: → Hated Across Weimar as Diktat
children.gloss: Condemned by all German parties; Tainted new Weimar Republic.

children.label: Fuelled Extremist Grievance Politics
children.gloss: Created deep national humiliation; Exploited during Great Depression.

children.label: Keynes, Dyson & Verdict
children.gloss: Keynes and cartoonist Will Dyson predicted disaster in 1919, while historians debate treaty harshness versus 1930s appeasement.

children.label: Keynes & Dyson’s 1940 Class Warning
children.gloss: Keynes quit over Carthaginian peace; Dyson drew weeping 1940 toddler.

children.label: Traditional: Treaty Caused Hitler
children.gloss: Bred economic ruin and bitterness; Undermined fragile Weimar democracy.

children.label: Modern: Allied Enforcement Failed
children.gloss: Left German industry, population intact; 1930s Allies failed to enforce.

children.label: → Unchecked Rearmament Led to 1939
children.gloss: Permitted aggressive Nazi expansion; Erupted into World War II.
